tasks.behavior: An email the provider refuses is set aside, and the other due emails still go out in the same round
acceptance: A Resend answer 400 or 422 (the message as sent, such as a bad address) records that event's failure with the usual backoff, and the round goes on to the next due event.
A 5xx, a timeout, 401, 403, 409 or 429 still ends the round as before (409 is a request in flight under the same key, which a retry settles).
Re-saving a refused payer address every 10 s no longer stops the other emails (the audit PoC as a test).
notes: 2026-10-19 review fail by reviewer: Blocker 1, notify.go:113-121: a refused event is given up at once (failed_at = now()). Accept 1 asks for the usual backoff, and R-115 was written to match the code instead. This is unsafe. Resend's errors page puts any bad request field under 400 validation_error, the from field too. EMAIL_FROM is an unchecked env var (config.go:106). One malformed EMAIL_FROM, or a deploy bug that breaks a field in every message (422 missing_required_field), now marks every due event failed, 20 per round, with no retry. Before, each event had 10 tries over about 4 h. Paid, settled, held, welcome and change emails have no way to start again. Fix: on ErrRefused, record the failure like other errors (attempts++, Backoff, failed_at at MaxAttempts) and return true so the round goes on. The payer PoC still holds: the PUT makes the receipt due again, and each round tries it once and moves on. Update R-115, docs/backend/api.md:69 and the ErrRefused comment (email.go:27, 'sending it again won't work' is false for a bad From). Minor: accept 1 says every 4xx except 401, 403 and 429 goes on; the code also stops on 409, 404, 405 and 451. 409 as a retry is fair (concurrent_idempotent_requests), but say why or follow the acceptance. Minor: R-115's first sentence is 37 words (D-84 says at most 25). Minor: api.md:70 moves 'Email off or no address' under the failed-send bullet; it is not about failures, holds two facts, and the line is 128 chars. Good: the transaction commits, Batch still bounds the round, a refused event leaves the due set, so there is no loop. Every kind (receipt, send, reminder, change, welcome) goes through deliverOne. Send and reminder history show failedAt (send.go:105). No address is logged. Both new tests fail without the fix. Ran: sh scripts/with-env.sh go test -count=1 ./internal/email/ ./internal/notify/ (both ok). Checked Resend's errors page for the status list.

2026-10-19 review pass by reviewer: No blockers. The earlier blocker is fixed. notify.go: a refused message (400 or 422) now records its failure like any other: attempts plus one, the same backoff, failed_at only at MaxAttempts. Only the round goes on. So a bad EMAIL_FROM no longer drops the queue at once; each event keeps its 10 tries over about 4 h. The send error has its own name, so the DB write can't hide it. The transaction commits. A refused event waits its backoff, so it leaves the due list and the round can't loop; Batch still bounds it. Every email kind goes through deliverOne. Send and reminder history show failedAt after the last try. No address is logged. The notify test fails without the fix (round 0 would send nothing). It checks one owner email per round over 3 rounds and the receipt waiting with attempts 1 and about 1 min backoff. The ErrRefused comment, acceptance 1 and 2, R-115 and api.md now match the code. api.md lines are under 120 chars. Minor: R-115's first sentence is 29 words, over D-84's 25. Minor: the test name still says 'SetsARefusedEmailAside', but the event is now retried. tasks.behavior: A user queues at most 20 client emails a day across all profiles: Send to client, reminders, retainer months and job changes
acceptance: Send to client answers 429 rate_limited once the user's profiles queued 20 client emails in 24 h, of any kind and from any profile.
Over the cap a reminder is not queued and goes out when there is room; a retainer month and a job change are still made, without the email.
The per-invoice and per-job limits stay; the old per-profile caps are replaced by the per-user cap.
PLAN lists an own email provider in place of Resend after the MVP; R-94, R-96, R-98, R-107 and api.md name the cap.

tasks.behavior: Requests with an unknown link or a bad body spend no shared limit, so junk traffic can't block Send to client or job acceptance
acceptance: The payer email route checks the body and finds the invoice before any limit; the shared email budget is spent only when a receipt is queued.
Job accept and change accept check the body and find a job that can still accept before the shared budget.
Forty junk requests to each route leave the owner's Send to client and a real client's accept working (the audit PoCs as tests).

tasks.behavior: Transactions CSV, the statement PDF and balance history stay bounded in memory, whatever a wallet receives
acceptance: The CSV and the statement read rows as they come instead of loading them all; the statement keeps only income lines.
A period with more than 10000 transactions answers 422 too_many_transactions, and the Export dialog says to pick a shorter period.
Balance history no longer loads every transfer row into memory.
With 100000 dust transfers, ten parallel exports stay far below the audit's 1.1 GB peak (the audit PoC as a test).

tasks.behavior: A payer-chooses invoice takes the option paid first only after every option's chain was read past that payment
acceptance: With a full payment on one chain and later dust on a chain the worker reads first, the full payment's option is chosen and paid; the dust is held.
Until every option's chain was scanned past the earliest transfer's block time, no option is chosen and no deposit of the invoice is booked.

tasks.behavior: An expired invoice whose balance the ledger can't explain is checked again after a growing wait, so such invoices can't use up a chain's round
acceptance: After an unexplained-balance alert the invoice is skipped until its wait ends (doubling, capped), unless a new confirmed deposit arrives.
With many such invoices, one round still marks an honest paid invoice paid (the audit PoC, scaled down, as a test).

tasks.behavior: Check status gives each invoice owner a share of the limit, so one account's invoices can't use it up for everyone
acceptance: Checks of one owner's invoices first take from that owner's own budget; once it is empty, payers of other owners' invoices still get checks.

tasks.behavior: The receipt lists only money paid to the creator; money held for the payer is not a payment
acceptance: Paid with 2 USDC, then 2 more: the receipt PDF lists one 2.00 payment.
A deposit split between the creator and held money lists only the creator's part; the pay page and receipt email follow the same rule or are named.

acceptance: A NUL, a bidi or control character, or x@bad..example answers 422 invalid_value, never 500; ordinary addresses still save.
